contract:
Write a Python module using PyTorch and Triton that defines fused_moe_experts(hidden_states, w13, w2, topk_weights, topk_ids) -> output for one mixture-of-experts layer.
Inputs, all on one CUDA device: hidden_states is a contiguous BF16 tensor shaped (tokens, hidden); w13 is BF16 shaped (experts, 2 * intermediate, hidden), whose first intermediate rows are the gate projection and last intermediate rows the up projection; w2 is BF16 shaped (experts, hidden, intermediate); topk_weights is FP32 shaped (tokens, top_k); topk_ids is INT32 shaped (tokens, top_k) with values in [0, experts). A token's top_k expert ids are distinct.
Result: output is a new BF16 tensor shaped (tokens, hidden) where, for each token t, output[t] = sum over j of topk_weights[t, j] * (silu(hidden_states[t] @ w13[e, :intermediate].T) * (hidden_states[t] @ w13[e, intermediate:].T)) @ w2[e].T with e = topk_ids[t, j]. Accumulate in FP32 and round to BF16 once at the end. Inputs must not be modified.
Tokens may number from 1 to a few thousand; small batches of 1 to 64 tokens matter most. Experts may receive no tokens or every token. A token's result must not depend on which other tokens share the batch beyond rounding, and the same inputs must give bit-identical results.
The GPU work must be done by your own Triton programs (@triton.jit). Importing torch is allowed only for tensor allocation, device handling, and reshaping or sorting token indices.
runtime_version_note: this integration replaces vLLM's Triton experts (TritonExperts.apply) for BF16 weights with SiLU activation and no expert map, bias, LoRA, or router weight on the input; any other vLLM version needs the hook reviewed again
